integrated_answer.claim: GET and POST /api/v1/accounts/:account_id/conversations/:conversation_id/labels map to index/create. The conversation controller permits conversation_id and labels: [] and selects @conversation as model; this is an array-shaped labels input, not nested label attributes.

The account base invokes current_account via EnsureCurrentAccountHelper. Conversation lookup uses Current.account.conversations.find_by!(display_id: params[:conversation_id]), then authorize @conversation, :show?. Access-token API calls additionally encounter the account API-enabled guard; complete membership, authentication and show? rules are outside the manifest.

POST calls update_labels(permitted_params[:labels]), which executes update!(label_list: labels), then reads label_list. It uses assignment rather than the separate add_labels helper, which combines existing and new labels. GET simply reads label_list. Replacement intent is inferred from assignment; exact normalization/persistence behavior is unverified.
Both Jbuilder templates use json.payload @labels: the response shape is {"payload": labels}. Exact runtime serialization was not exercised.

Account label CRUD is separate: /api/v1/accounts/:account_id/labels exposes index/show/create/update/destroy, invokes check_authorization, policy-scopes index, fetches/creates through Current.account.labels, and permits required nested label fields title, description, color, show_on_sidebar. Destroy deletes the record and enqueues Labels::RemoveAssociationsJob. This does not establish which label titles conversation assignment ultimately accepts.

The request-spec file declares four examples: unauthenticated GET/POST return unauthorized; an account agent added as inbox_member succeeds for GET/POST using conversation.display_id. GET checks label1/label2 response substrings; POST checks label3/label4 substrings. These assertions do not prove the exact payload structure or removal of prior labels, and no tests ran.

findings_or_risks.claim: One justified unverified gap: this request-spec file has no authenticated cross-account/inaccessible-conversation denial example. Account-scoped lookup and authorize invocation provide source evidence of boundaries, but the listed tests do not verify denial. This is a coverage gap, not a demonstrated defect.
